CausalChain: Green tea catechins (EGCG) administration -> modulation of mitochondrial function in cancer stem cells -> increased mitochondrial ROS generation -> suppression of IL-8 signaling -> selective induction of apoptosis in cancer stem cells -> reduction in metastatic potential
Hypothesis: Targeted delivery of green tea catechins, particularly EGCG, to cancer stem cells increases mitochondrial oxidative stress and downregulates IL-8 signaling, thereby selectively inducing apoptosis in these cells and reducing metastatic potential in aggressive cancers.
Abstract: Recent evidence underscores the multifaceted actions of green tea catechins, especially EGCG, on key cellular mechanisms including mitochondrial function, redox balance, and inflammatory signaling. In particular, data reveal that EGCG modulates pathways such as IL-8 signaling and oxidative phosphorylation in cancer stem cells, which are pivotal in tumor metastasis. We propose that targeted delivery of EGCG to cancer stem cells can amplify mitochondrial oxidative stress beyond their limited antioxidant capacity, thereby selectively triggering apoptosis in these cells. This strategy may synergize with mitochondrial pro-oxidant therapies to reduce the metastatic potential of aggressive cancers without affecting normal cells.
